unverifiable_exemptions: Inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care, and detention or correctional facilities are not residential dwelling units
coverage.summary: Applies in Jersey City to any real estate lessor that owns real property and leases any part of it as a residential dwelling unit. A residential dwelling unit is any house, apartment, accessory unit or other unit intended as a person's primary residence. Inpatient medical care, licensed long-term care and detention or correctional facilities are excluded. The text sets no unit-count, building-age or landlord-size limits.

result.notes:
Two fields were set to null because they describe conduct, not which buildings, units or owners are covered:
- owner_conditions: the definition exempts owners of multiple properties only for actions related exclusively to their own properties. This narrows the coordination conduct, not the class of owners.
- other_conditions: the licensed real estate agent carve-out limits who counts as a service provider, not which properties are covered.

requires_unknown_facts is set to false because the rule reaches ordinary residential rental units. The excluded facility types are listed as unverifiable exemptions; licensure and facility status may not be visible in assessor data.

Chapter 218's separate 'Exempt dwellings' section (renumbered § 218-13) is marked unchanged and its text is not in the documents. It is unknown whether it limits § 218-12.

The possible FAIR Act preemption raised in conflict_note is not supported by any provided document, so supersedes_state_rule, yields_to_local_rule and may_preempt_local_rules remain null.
